title: A 27B coding model, one AMD card, and the setting that gives you 2.25x for free
headings: The finding: MTP is a pure win, not a trade-off
The tuning payoff: cap the thinking budget
summary: Published write-up of Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M (dense) on one 32 GB R9700 under llama.cpp Vulkan b9950, comparing an MTP-on (unsloth) and an MTP-off (jackrong) GGUF build plus a reasoning-budget sweep. Setup: 14 agentic-coding tasks (11 deterministic, 3 blind-judged), reps=1, shallow prompts of about 50-100 tokens. Headline: MTP on decodes 70.3 tok/s vs 31.1 (2.25x) at 100% deterministic accuracy, and a thinking cap of 512-2048 cut tokens and latency 40-55% with 0% runaways vs 7.1% uncapped.
status_note: reps=1 and shallow ~50-100-token prompts only; 10-50K agentic-depth rerun pending

summary: Post-mortem article on four assumptions checked against the Qwen3.6-27B reasoning-budget and MTP sweep (llama.cpp Vulkan b9950, R9700, 14 tasks, reps=1, shallow prompts), each with a follow-up or grading check. Headline: --reasoning-budget 0 is uncapped on this build (1,736 thinking tokens vs 1,262 at its own rb2048), and the 7.1% uncapped runaway rate is the same across all three draft settings. headings: The trust beat: how we know we didn't fool ourselves
summary: Write-up of the Qwen3.6-27B reasoning-budget sweep (MTP on and off, llama.cpp Vulkan b9950, R9700, 14 tasks, reps=1, shallow prompts), centred on how the result was checked. Headline: a cap of 512-2048 keeps 100% deterministic accuracy and cuts tokens and latency 40-55%, with runaways at 7.1% uncapped vs 0% capped. title: dp-forge brief review+fix (W2-06..08) - Swift-1.5 heretic vs RedHat MXFP4 (DFlash2, Sly 1.8.1 and 1.9.1) vs Opus, and the Cactus loop fix
takeaway: On an agentic brief review+fix task, RedHat MXFP4 failed at Sly's default Cactus δ 0.5 (9 runaway thinking loops, 0/3 briefs in 3 h) because the lossy spec-decode acceptance locks in repetition; with CACTUS_DELTA=0 it ran W2-08 loop-free and out-reviewed heretic (9/19 vs 4/19 Opus findings blind, 2 reasoned rejections, own lint-clean fix) at 29-38 % slower decode and ~9x the time (6.8x the generated tokens x 1.35x slower decode, plus 6 compactions fed by the template's reasoning replay; not context size, not literal repetition). Rerun on Sly 1.9.1 (δ 0.5 + fade/cap, template v22.5-sly2 that drops old reasoning, budget RUNBOOK): W2-08 in 87 min (-22 %), 2 compactions instead of 6, decode 102 tok/s, all 6 high Opus findings fixed with a clean probe - but the blind review collapsed to 1/19 (no probes) and 3 decision loops returned (one to the output cap); the template alone cuts prompt tokens 25 % (calculated on the δ 0 session). Added 2026-10-31: unsloth Q4_K_XL on llama-swap (sharp template) found 12/19 blind (high 3/6) vs RedHat δ 0's 9/19 (4/6) under one blind re-grade - grey zone at n = 1; the re-grade also turned one RedHat δ 0 extra finding to wrong (precision 13/14). Then RedHat δ 0 with only the chat template swapped to sharp: 11/19 (high 4/6, 14/14) with 38 % less thinking and 35 % fewer tool calls - no quality loss, +2 not significant; template held equal, Q4_K_XL vs RedHat is a tie (12 vs 11, 4-way blind grade).

title: unsloth Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL on llama-swap (sharp template) vs RedHat MXFP4 δ 0 vs heretic - W2-08 blind review quality, blind-graded against the 19 Opus findings
takeaway: On the W2-08 blind review (RUNBOOK step A, n = 1 per config, one blind grader for all three) Q4_K_XL found 12/19 Opus findings (high 3/6, 15/15 findings real) vs RedHat δ 0's 9/19 (high 4/6, 13/14) and heretic's 4/19 (high 3/6). The +3 is inside the pre-registered grey zone (3-4), so no quality difference is demonstrated - Q4_K_XL is broader (5/6 lows), RedHat stronger on highs and probe fidelity; Q4_K_XL missed high #6 because its lint probe did not copy the brief verbatim. Q4_K_XL got there with half the thinking (242k vs 489k chars) and 71 vs 156 tool calls, but its template adds a terseness directive to v22.5 (the only template difference, MEASURED diff) and the engine differs, so that is not attributable to the model. The follow-up RedHat + sharp-template run (campaigns/agentic/2026-10-31-0000-redhat-sharp-w208-blind) found 11/19 (high 4/6) with 304k thinking chars / 101 tool calls: with the template equal the two models tie, and most of the efficiency edge was the template. A second Q4_K_XL rep remains the noise check.

title: Analysis: why Q4_K_XL "thought less", and where the quality + speed headroom is (W2-08 agentic runs, R9700)
takeaway: Q4_K_XL did not think less per step. Thinking per tool call was 3.0-3.6k chars in all four W2-08 arms (Q4 3,453; RedHat 1.8.1+sharp 3,043; 1.9.1+sharp 3,641; old template 3,154). Q4 took fewer steps (70 vs 80/100 tool calls) and read fewer distinct files (15 vs 18/25), and the two near-identical RedHat δ 0 runs already differ by 20% in steps, so at n = 1 no parameter can be blamed (W4 quantization does not lengthen reasoning, T1). Every run auto-compacted at 136-143k (Claude Code window 180000 × 85%, servers accept 260-262k), costing 327-614 s per run (10-22% of the window) and 109-122k tokens of context per event. Best levers: move the compaction window (speed + quality), spend the speed headroom on a second independent review (union +2…+5 weighted points, 3 runs → 29/38 vs best single 23), and fix three findings no config ever found in the review protocol. δ 0.3 decodes +51% (84.2 vs 55.8 tok/s), but its only run skipped the blind review (its 15.8% repeated-line signal is repeated import lines, not a loop; corrected 17:45).

title: Analysis: how much old reasoning is reused, the sharp and buun templates, and why Cactus δ 0.5 loops (W2-08 agentic transcripts, R9700)
takeaway: Transcript-only analysis of seven W2-08 agentic runs (no GPU). (1) Old reasoning is rarely needed. Only 3.4-6.7% of the identifiers a step emits existed solely in thinking two or more steps back, and a keep-newest (k=1) run re-derives 3.6% on its own. A blind judge rated 6 of 32 keep-all reuse cases real dependencies, all from a running findings ledger (2 of them risky), and 0 of 8 in the k=1 run. A written conclusion of ≤15% would have kept everything later steps used in 7 of 10 blocks; the block's own last paragraph in only 2 of 10. → k=1 plus an externalized findings ledger. (2) "sharp" is a third-party template: froggeric v22.5 plus a 3-line TERSENESS system block. Its measured effect is −35-38% work with no demonstrated quality change (+2 findings, below the pre-registered ≥5) and weaker severity calibration. Five clauses can over-reach in an agent run; a scoped wording is proposed for an A/B. (3) The buun Qwen3.6 template disables thinking whenever tools are present by default, and blanks thinking after two short error-looking tool results (our tsc/eslint probes trigger it). Not usable as-is. (4) Cactus δ0.5 loops are inherent to its lossy acceptance rule, not a code bug. On 1.8.1 any drafted token with target p ≥ 0.5 is accepted with certainty, so a loop has no exit (0 of 3 top loops escaped, all hit 64k). The 1.9.1 cap restores half the stock escape, but 4 of the 6 measured 1.9.1 loop onsets were before the fade start (4,096 tokens). Under the cap, δ0.3 equals δ0.5 for every drafted token with p ≥ 0.29. (5) Correction: δ0.3's "15.8% loop signal" was repeated import lines, not a loop; δ 0 runs show 13.8-15.8% repeated-line blocks with no loop either.

problems.problem: The 27B long-context prefill falls to a legacy kernel at about one third of the fast throughput past 32,768 tokens
problems.cause: the WMMA prefill envelope was certified on a model with 8 heads and 2 KV heads; this 27B has 24 and 4, and nothing at runtime says so
problems.fix: developer.flash_prefill 1 with developer.flash_prefill_min_ctx 1000000; re-certify the ceiling for 24/4 shapes (proposed)
problems.where: 3.1 The prefill blocker, and the fix

problems.problem: flash_prefill on its own collapses decode to 6.7 tok/s
problems.cause: the global opt-in also covers the DFlash verify forward, which falls to a scalar kernel with 48 workgroups on a 64-CU part
problems.fix: pair it with flash_prefill_min_ctx 1000000 (decode recovers to 21.9 tok/s)

problems.problem: memory.cask.enabled = false does not disable CASK; DFlash silently fell to legacy capped mode at about 6.4x coding decode cost
problems.cause: the draft code branches on whether a sidecar path is configured, not on eviction being enabled
problems.fix: hipfire config unset memory.cask.sidecar

problems.problem: A CASK win on the old ROCm became a 47% prefill loss after the upgrade
problems.cause: driver upgrade changed the tuning outcome
problems.fix: re-measure every tuning decision after a driver upgrade

problems.problem: speculation.mode = auto selects almost nothing; a forced global mode destroys the other model's speculator
problems.cause: precedence is structural (DSpark > DFlash > MTP > n-gram)
problems.fix: per-model overlays instead of a global speculation.mode

problems.problem: The VMM KV backend hides VRAM contention as slowdown with nothing in any log; one early result was invalid because llama-swap held 30,343 of 32,624 MB
problems.cause: the backend pages instead of failing when VRAM is taken
problems.fix: gate every run on exclusive GPU access before loading
problems.where: 5.3 The VMM KV backend hides contention instead of failing

problems.problem: Draft-free boots fault in gemm_gate_up_mq4g256v2_wmma_gfx12_bt12; the daemon wedges and /health keeps answering ok, so requests hang until kill -9
problems.cause: first large matmul on a draft-free memory layout; a warm-up big enough to trigger it would itself fault; a second model faulted in another gfx12 WMMA GEMM
problems.fix: no configuration-level workaround; upstream report with the 7-of-19 reproduction; a liveness probe that exercises the GPU plus restart-on-fault
problems.where: 4.1 The GPU memory fault that reports itself healthy

problems.problem: A cold page cache hangs model load: the loader stalls at layers 50-54 of 64 for 15 minutes
problems.cause: a CPU spin in the loader (one core pinned, no disk movement), not slow I/O; three theories falsified
problems.fix: prime the page cache with a sequential read before boot (27B boot 95 s); not sufficient for the 20 GB muse model
problems.where: 4.2 Cold page cache hangs the model load

problems.problem: Identical decode runs spread 1.9x (16.2 to 30.4 tok/s without speculation)
problems.cause: card power management, per the clock trace
problems.fix: no decode claim from fewer than about five runs, reported with spread
problems.where: 4.3 Run-to-run spread makes single runs worthless

problems.problem: The default 30,000 ms queue timeout drops excess concurrent work with HTTP 503 (2 of 4 6.5k requests, 3 of 4 26k requests)
problems.cause: queue_timeout_ms default drops instead of queueing; continuous batching also caps a lane at 15,872 tokens
problems.fix: serve.queue_timeout_ms 0

problems.problem: The hipfire rows generate non-reasoning output (reasoning.effort xhigh dropped) while the llama.cpp rows expose thinking variants
problems.cause: thinking disabled in hipfire loads
problems.fix: wall-time comparisons are made against llama.cpp's non-thinking arm

problems.problem: hipfire cannot express context depth, KV mode, sampling or speculation on its command line; llama-swap integration needed a separate builder and guards
problems.cause: settings live in config.toml, overlays and the request body
problems.fix: separate command builder, a no-shared-macro rule, and guards that refuse llama.cpp-only keys

problems.problem: Multi-agent work forces a full re-prefill per switch (about 7 minutes at 73k)
problems.cause: one conversation_tokens sequence; DeltaNet state cannot be rewound to an earlier position
problems.fix: none by setting; per-conversation KV checkpoints proposed
problems.where: 3.6 The cache that is not a cache

problems.problem: A configured CASK sidecar disables prefix caching entirely; truncated assistant turns are not stored for splice
problems.cause: sidecar configuration and token-cap truncation
problems.fix: unset the sidecar; reuse across a truncated turn depends on re-tokenisation being stable
problems.where: 9b. Late results that changed the conclusions

problems.problem: A vendor headline of 258 tok/s came from a synthetic prompt at tau 13.11; real prose gave tau 1.7-2.2 and lost to plain decoding past 55k
problems.cause: synthetic prompt shape
problems.fix: measure speculation on the output shape it will actually see

problems.problem: A false regression was announced: ROCm 10 supposedly broke DFlash on coding workloads
problems.cause: a conclusion written before its control arm was run
problems.fix: retracted; control arm run; the lesson is to run the control first

title: Benchmark: deep-context 35B-A3B to 200K tokens — depth curve · MTP × depth · q8_0 confirm · parallel at the ceiling — R9700 (gfx1201)
takeaway: Deep-context 35B on Vulkan to 200K tokens (native 262144 cap). f16 KV runs to 200K with no OOM — VRAM is not binding, the RoPE cap is. Prefill decays 3077→1254 tok/s and decode 104→61 (8K→200K). **MTP grows with depth (+14→+35% decode) but is a NET LOSS for deep-prefill/short-decode** (200K: +18s prefill vs +1s decode saved → −17s wall). **q8_0 KV is catastrophic at depth: −40% prefill, −22% decode, TTFT +66%** (penalty scales with ctx) → keep f16 everywhere. Parallel at 32K prompts is prefill-bound: np2→np4 doubles TTFT (24→49s) for ~0 aggregate gain.

title: Benchmark: 27B dense — f16 & q8_0 max-context ceilings + first 40K-depth throughput — R9700 (gfx1201)
takeaway: ⚠️ CORRECTED — the "64K f16 / 120K q8_0 ceiling" conclusion below is WRONG. Qwen3.6-27B is a HYBRID arch (only 16 of 65 blocks are full-attention; 48 are SSM/linear-attn with no growing KV), so f16 KV is 64 KiB/tok not 260, and the real max is ~240K (f16) / native 262K (q8_0). MEASURED 2026-07-12: 200K f16 loaded in 31s using 29.0 GiB VRAM. The 64K/120K figures were the highest TESTED, never the ceiling. STILL VALID (MEASURED at 40K depth): prefill ~742 tok/s f16 / ~635 q8_0 (−14%), decode flat ~28.5 tok/s, TTFT 54s/63s. Superseded by docs/plans/2026-07-12-27b-finetune-quality-tokens.md + hybrid-aware bench/core/gguf_kv.py.

title: 27B serving substrate — real prefill curve, KV f16/q8_0, MTP decode, cache reuse (R9700)
takeaway: The "slow prefill" was a small-input artifact — real prefill at depth is 666–831 tok/s (3–4× the 75-token number) and sags with depth. Prompt-cache reuse cuts 32K ttft 42.7s→3.1s (13.7×) — the big agentic win (built-in; explicit --cache-reuse flags add nothing). KV q8_0 REJECTED (−12%/−19% prefill for ~0 decode gain). MTP = 2.0× decode for −5% prefill + ~1.4 GiB. ROCm/HIP ~92× slower prefill than Vulkan on gfx1201 (8 vs 756 tok/s). Frozen substrate for Campaign 2: vulkan · f16 · MTP-on.
headings: Legend — knobs & labels in this run
KV decision — q8_0 REJECTED (≤5% rule, decisively)
summary: Campaign 1 of 3: a 10-probe engine-bench on Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-Q4_K_M (Vulkan b9950, ctx 65536, np 1) measured the real prefill curve at 8K, 32K and 64K, KV f16 vs q8_0, MTP on/off, prefix-cache reuse, plus two follow-ups (cache-reuse flags, ROCm/HIP spot-check at 32K). A warm 32K prefix cuts time-to-first-token from 42.66 s to 3.12 s (13.7x), and ROCm/HIP prefill runs at about 8.1 tok/s against Vulkan's 756 tok/s (about 92x slower). q8_0 KV is rejected (prefill −11.8% at 32K), MTP doubles decode (27.8 to 55.2 tok/s) for a −5.2% prefill tax, and Vulkan f16 with MTP on is the frozen substrate for Campaign 2.

title: Analysis: the penalty-sampler tax — what actually costs `presence_penalty` its 30% (and what MTP has to do with it) — R9700 (gfx1201)
takeaway: **Corrects the 27b-vs-35b campaign's `presence_penalty × MTP` mechanism.** Enabling ANY penalty sampler (presence/frequency/repeat) costs a **fixed ~2 ms/token of host work** — MEASURED +1.95/+2.07/+1.97 ms/tok across 35B-MTP-on/off and 27B-dense, and **CONFIRMED at ~132.9k depth (+1.3–1.9 ms/tok, depth-invariant)** — while draft acceptance is **unchanged**: `pp=0.01` emits a **sha1-identical** reply with identical draft counts and acceptance to the decimal, yet loses ~30% decode. Not an MTP interaction — MTP just shortens the step so the same fixed tax eats a bigger fraction (Amdahl). The campaign's implied +4.16 ms/tok was a **pp=1.5** figure that stacks the fixed tax **plus** genuine draft rejection at high penalty (the minority component the campaign over-generalized to the whole effect); the pure tax is ~2 ms at every depth, not 4, and session-degradation is excluded. `min_p` is free; `top_k 40`/`top_p 1.0` ~free. Also: `--spec-draft-n-max` 2–3 optimal shallow AND at depth (n-max 8 → 80 t/s, *worse than MTP off*), **MTP is not output-preserving** (on/off diverge at a fixed seed), and **MTP costs ~84 MiB GTT** — a lead on the campaign's unattributed spill.

summary: A hand-driven scouting probe on llama.cpp b9950 Vulkan (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MTP on/off and Qwen3.6-27B, ctx 4096, n=1-2 on most cells, plus a ~132.9k-token depth confirm) tested why enabling presence_penalty costs decode, and refutes the earlier campaign's presence_penalty x MTP interaction claim. The mechanism is a fixed ~2 ms/token host cost of enabling any penalty sampler (+1.95, +2.07, +1.97 ms/tok across three configs), which hurts most on the fastest step: at presence_penalty 0.01 the reply is sha1-identical with identical draft acceptance (69.06%), yet decode falls 28.6% (161.1 to 115.1 tok/s). Also measured: --spec-draft-n-max 3 is optimal, n-max 8 (80.2 t/s) is worse than MTP off (107.6 t/s), and MTP is not output-preserving.

title: 27B quality tuning — reasoning-budget is the master economy knob
takeaway: On the frozen Vulkan/f16 substrate at the corrected **temp 0.6**, `--reasoning-budget` is the master quality/economy knob: capping at **~1024 tok** keeps **100% deterministic accuracy** and peak LLM-judge quality (unsloth **4.83/5**, jackrong 4.56) while cutting tokens/latency **40–55%** and giving **0% runaways**. `512` starves design/review tasks. Two traps: **`--reasoning-budget 0` = uncapped, NOT no-think** (jackrong rb0 = most thinking, 1736 tok); and the **7.1% runaways are an uncapped-budget pathology, NOT MTP-draft tuning** — ⚠️ **CORRECTED 2026-07-16**: MTP draft params (`--spec-draft-p-min`/`-n-max`) are *live* but gate draft *depth/speed*, not reasoning *length* (MEASURED, `campaigns/perf/2026-07-16-0927-mtp-sampler-tax/results/2026-07-16-1111-spec-draft-pmin-mtp/`), so they cannot drive the runaway — which is a constant 7.1% across all three *uncapped* B4 cells and 0% on every *capped* one, with the 91% det an n=1 reshuffle. Keep MTP-draft params at default; **the runaway fix is the budget cap**. **unsloth-MTP is the better substrate** (2.25× decode, top quality). Best config: unsloth-MTP + `--reasoning-budget 1024`–`2048` @ temp 0.6 (2048 as depth-safe default). ⚠️ Tuned on shallow prompts + reps=1 — the decision-blocking gap is **quality at 10–50K agentic depth + multi-turn tool-use** (Phase 3/4), not the 3 skipped low-value configs.

title: Qwen3.6-27B quality-at-depth — per-task deep dive (R9700)
takeaway: Per-task deep dive. The 27B sits in the haiku->sonnet band (best cells 92-99% on deep-equal/store-remove); the REAL wall is strict eslint/tsc (lint 0.29, types 0.32), NOT logic (tests 0.89, edge 0.95). Reasoning budget helps at 64k, saturates at 128k (model never early-stops). KV q8 fine on average but tanks lru-cache and destabilises output at 128k (think-tag leaks/truncation). Fastest-good config: un-d64-f16-rb2048. DATA VALIDITY: the run's original grade was voided by a vitest execution fault (tests+edge=0 on all 120) — EXCLUDED from all analysis here; every number uses a clean CPU-only re-grade of the same saved answers. Harness fix + rerun steps in §1.

summary: Per-task deep dive on the same 120 frozen Qwen3.6-27B answers (6 TypeScript-TDD tasks, 10 configs, reps=2) after the original grade was voided by a vitest execution fault that zeroed tests and edge on every reply. A CPU-only re-grade of the saved answers gives per-cell TS 67-79% (not 24-33%): the 27B sits in the haiku-to-sonnet band, reaching 92-99% on deep-equal and store-remove, while strict eslint (mean 0.29) and tsc (0.32) are the real wall, not logic (tests 0.89, edge 0.95). Budget helps at 64k (68, 75, 79% at 1024, 2048, 4096) and is flat at 128k (68, 73, 73%); q8 KV is -2% on average at 128k but collapses lru-cache (78 to 47) and destabilises expr-eval on jackrong, so un-d64-f16-rb2048 (75% mean, about 50-70 s generation) is the recommended robust config.

title: Recommendation — top configs for an agentic dev system (100k ctx) — R9700 (gfx1201)
takeaway: Top agentic configs at ~100k ctx, R9700: **27B Q4_K_M f16** (TS 78.3, 46.1 t/s, budget 4096), **27B Q6_K** (TS 80.9, 32.6 t/s), **35B-A3B** (TS 77.5, 120.1 t/s, budget 16384); quant ladder is a statistical null (max |t| 1.98 < 2.776), 35B is 2.6–3.7× faster.

summary: Operator-facing recommendation of three configs for an agentic TypeScript loop at about 100k context on the R9700: 27B Q4_K_M f16 at reasoning budget 4096 (TS 78.3), 27B Q6_K q8_0 at budget 4096 (TS 80.9), and 35B-A3B Q4_K_M f16 at budget 16384 (TS 77.5), each with a full llama-server launch and a per-request sampling block. Numbers are measured at about 133k depth, so at 100k VRAM is an upper bound and speed a lower bound.

title: Hardest tasks at 128k — 27B quant ladder, reasoning budget, and 35B-A3B sampling (R9700)
takeaway: 14 cells x 5 tasks x 3 reps = 210 replies at ~132.9k tokens. Three axes, one clear answer each. QUANT: bounded null — Q4_K_M 78.3, Q4_K_XL 69.8, Q5_K_M 76.5, Q6_K 80.9 TS%, no paired delta significant, design resolves only >=12 pts; the accidental KV control (Q5_K_M f16 74.3 vs q8_0 76.5) bounds the README's KV confound as negligible. BUDGET: 4096 to 16384 buys +0.3 pts on the 27B (t=0.37, ns) for +60s; above ~4k the budget stops binding — 14 of 15 35B replies are IDENTICAL between 16384 and unlimited, and the one reply unlimited freed ran away to 31,093 think tokens and fell 77 to 45. Refutes our own sourced hypothesis that truncated thinking drives the wall. The MoE, unlike the dense 27B, DOES benefit from a bigger budget (35B rb4096 vs rb16384 -4.3, t=-5.45, SIGNIFICANT — surfaced by the 2026-07-16 --baseline re-analysis). SAMPLING (35B): temp 0.6 (Qwen's coding recipe) is the best point at 77.5; use the recipe WHOLE. CORRECTED 2026-07-16 (re-baselined within-model): temp 0.3's "significant" deficit was a wrong-baseline artifact and is WITHDRAWN (-7.5, t=-2.60, ns); only the whole general-mode preset survives (-15.4, t=-3.41). The presence_penalty>0 presets lose ~30-40% decode — but the mechanism ("pp breaks MTP acceptance") is REFUTED: it is a fixed ~2 ms/tok host tax on the penalties sampler, no MTP interaction, acceptance untouched (see docs/findings/llamacpp/2026-07-16-0927-mtp-sampler-tax.md). STABLE: the wall is cleanliness (lint 0.36, types 0.47) not logic (tests 0.84, reuse 0.99); 35B is ~2.6-3.7x faster to a full answer; reruns pay (delta rerun +4.6..+17.5). GTT spill 1551-2841 MiB in ALL 14 cells. References are NOT depth-matched (~213x shallower) — no bare local-vs-reference delta is a capability gap.

title: Ornith-1.0-35B vs Qwen3.6-35B-A3B vs Gemma-4-31B at 120k depth (Gemma needs ROCm)
takeaway: Ornith-1.0-35B (qwen35moe hybrid, MTP off, Vulkan) on the hardest-tasks TS-TDD suite at ~120k depth, 3 reps: **62.2% TS** (MEASURED), 1/5 hard-pass, decode 70.9 t/s, fits clean at f16 (25.4 GiB). Vs Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at MATCHED settings (n=3): 35B is **73.3%** (Δ−11.0, paired t=−1.16 → NOT significant), but Ornith is **~half as noisy** (within-task sd 7.4 vs 12.9), wins the two stable tasks (expr-eval/async-memo), and its ~2× speed deficit is **MTP-only** (Ornith has 0 nextn). **Gemma-4-31B: Vulkan/RADV DEVICE-LOSTS at deep prefill and crashes the GUI (~65k @ctx163840 / ~24.5k @140000) — a driver bug, NOT memory — but on `BACKEND=rocm` it runs the full depth suite CLEAN** (q8_0, ctx150000, n=1): **56.6% TS, 0/5 hard-pass, decode 11.6 t/s** (ROCm ~6× slower decode; prefill ~650→200 t/s, so the old ~92× figure is wrong). Gemma hits the lint/types wall harder than Ornith (0.12/0.20) and emits `<think>` (capture.py splits fine). Ornith leads Gemma ~62 vs ~57 but Gemma n=1 (CI [33,80]) is not yet a real comparison.

title: runner-simplify validation + multi-model benchmark
takeaway: runner-simplify harness change is **outcome-neutral** (119 runs); **between-block variance** outweighs every model/arm difference. Local default: `Brian6145/27B-Q4_K_M` for statement-driven work, `unsloth/35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M` for contract-/test-bearing work — complementary, not ranked. `ThinkingCap-27B-Q6_K_L` posted the best attempts/wall yet silently overwrote translations: **gate-green is not a quality proxy**.

summary: runner-simplify validation plus a multi-model benchmark on the agentic code runner: nine phase-1 tasks and the 2035-line T010 task, with two Claude arms (BASE = Opus via speckit, SIM = Sonnet on the runner payload) as the production bar. The three transferred runner-simplify commits are outcome-neutral on T010 (true-green 5/5 vs 5/6, wall gap 102 s, t=0.80). Between-block variance (Brian6145 27B wall +78 % between blocks) exceeds every model or arm difference, so no ranking from one block or one sample is safe. LLM-judge verdicts show gate-green is not a quality proxy: ThinkingCap-27B-Q6_K_L had the most favourable operational numbers but overwrote working Hungarian translations in 4 of 5 samples.

title: KLD: Qwen3.8-27B, 15 quant × engine arms, teacher-forced against Q8_0 (R9700, gfx1201)
takeaway: Qwen3.8-27B, 15 arms scored teacher-forced against a Q8_0 reference (128 prompts × 32 positions, fixed scorer). UD-Q6_K on llama.cpp is the closest production-config arm (KL 0.0045, round 3), IQ4R-L-V4 on radiance is next (0.0079, resolved above Q6), then UD-Q4_K_XL (0.0164); swapping llama.cpp's q8_0 KV for f16 shows no KV cost (Q6 unresolved; Q4_K_XL f16 slightly further, +0.0009), and every MXFP4 arm sits at 0.056–0.066 whatever the engine; heretic is 0.089. Floors: llama.cpp re-run 0.0018, vLLM and radiance re-boots bit-identical. DFlash, radiance 1.11→1.17 and Sly 1.8.1→1.11.0 are not resolved from noise; the int4 lm head costs 0.0045 (resolved). Round 2 (d on Sly 1.8.1) puts heretic's extra +0.022 on the model, not the engine.

title: vllm-radiance on the R9700 (gfx1201) — what it is, what transfers to a single-GPU INT4 setup
takeaway: `stilldeadcode/vllm-radiance` (gfx1201-only vLLM 0.27.1 + libr4d kernels) is the undisclosed "tuned" build behind Puget's R9700 numbers, and it runs our single-GPU INT4 checkpoint. **Clean 4-depth curve on ONE fixture family (findings 21-22): llama.cpp + MTP wins decode at every depth by 9-33 %; radiance's only win is prefill/TTFT at 8k.** Radiance decode does NOT decay with depth (exponent +0.070, R2 0.25) - the earlier "degrades with depth" claim was a content artifact and is withdrawn. The ranking is set by WORKLOAD, not depth: radiance leads on generated code, llama.cpp on review prose. A divergent-tail warm test (finding 23) confirms partial cache hits equal full hits, so the earlier identical-prompt warm figures stand.
headings: Results (MEASURED, pp2048 / tg150, concurrency 1, warmup + 3 runs)
Caveat on the R4 decode figure
Recommended config (single R9700, INT4, from the image README adapted to one GPU)

summary: stilldeadcode vllm-radiance (vLLM 0.27.1 with the libr4d gfx1201 kernels) run on one R9700 with a W4A16 Qwen3.8-27B checkpoint, against host vLLM 0.29.0 and llama.cpp Vulkan with MTP. Configured per its README, radiance gives +22.7 % prefill at decode parity without MTP; with MTP8 and its drafter patches it reaches 35.0 tok/s decode (n=3, host baseline 17.6). On one fixture family with MTP on both engines, llama.cpp decodes faster at every depth from 8k to 32k (9-33 %). The winner at the same 8k depth flips with workload, and the earlier depth-degradation claim was a fixture artifact (withdrawn). Prefix caching gives 17.4x TTFT on byte-identical 32k prompts.
status_note: R5 (fp8 KV) and R6 (prefix-cache/align) are still pending in the results table, yet the recommended config uses both settings. Finding 8 says OPEN although finding 12 tested the flag. Finding 16 still states the withdrawn depth-degradation claim. Finding 19 (llama.cpp warm TTFT 0.43 s, llama.cpp wins) conflicts with finding 23 (radiance owns the warm case, 2.41 vs 3.34 s).

title: Benchmark: Ornith 1.5 on native Radiance vs Sly (Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.5-35B) — R9700 (gfx1201)
takeaway: Best 35B on one R9700 at 210 W is Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B w4a8 on native Radiance 1.16.0 with MTP K=3: 220/205/175 t/s decode and 13059/8029/5301 t/s prefill at 10k/50k/100k, 2.1-2.5x Qwen3.8-27B on Sly 1.9.1 (87/96/82 t/s). Ornith on Sly with Radiance's serving values and DFlash K=3 reaches only 95/71/67 t/s, and MTP does not load there on any usable backend. The Qwen3.5-35B slowdown on Sly is the EMULATION MoE backend (16.6 to 110 t/s with triton_unfused). Radiance's default 96 MiB headroom crashed the desktop once, and coding quality is untested.
summary: One-off comparison of Ornith 1.5 w4a8 on native Radiance 1.16.0 (MTP K=3) with Ornith 1.5 MXFP4 on Sly 1.9.1 (DFlash K=3; MTP fails to load), Qwen3.8-27B on Sly (DFlash2 K=7) and Qwen3.5-35B on Sly (DFlash K=7, with the triton_unfused and EMULATION MoE backends), at 10k/50k/100k cold-prefill depth with 3 requests per cell, 256 output tokens, temperature 1.0. title: ROCm `-fa on` → HSA memory fault on gfx1201 — kernel evidence & attribution
takeaway: Every ROCm bench with `-fa on` crashes with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`; `sudo dmesg` confirms a real GPU page **permission** fault in `llama-bench` (PERMISSION_FAULTS=0x3, MAPPING_ERROR=0 — not OOM/contention). Reproduced twice (bench run + isolated test on a free GPU) and identically on both the 10.0 and 10.1 runtimes; `-fa off` is clean. No matching upstream issue found (4 searches, 2026-10-07). Kernel diff -34→-38 (done): six amdkfd/SVM/userq-fence patches landed in that window — one **gfx12-specific** (`6c1f4f7`, EOP interrupt routing) — a coherent suspect set for the signature. Attribution test = reboot to 7.0.0-34 (installed). ROCm bench arms are blocked until resolved; `latest-rocm` stays on the 10.0 build per user decision.
headings: Register decode (INFERRED — standard amdgpu fault-status semantics)
summary: Root-cause investigation of an HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT that aborts llama-bench on the ROCm arm whenever flash attention is on (-fa on), using dmesg fault registers, an isolation matrix (free GPU, -fa off, Vulkan control, ROCm 10.0 vs 10.1), an upstream search and a kernel 7.0.0-34 vs 7.0.0-38 changelog diff. Main result: the fault is a GPU permission fault on a mapped page (PERMISSION_FAULTS=0x3, MAPPING_ERROR=0), it reproduces identically on the ROCm 10.0 and 10.1 runtimes, and it is absent with -fa off; the first suspect is kernel 7.0.0-38 (six amdkfd/SVM/userq commits), but the reboot test that would attribute it to the driver is still pending.

title: Benchmark: vLLM 0.29.0 attention backends on Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 — R9700 (gfx1201)
takeaway: vLLM 0.29.0 + RedHatAI Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 on the R9700 — the default ROCm attention backend collapses decode at depth (**2.8 tok/s @32k**); `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` fixes it (**14.1 tok/s**, +10% at 512 too) but costs 32k prefill (**222 vs ~470 tok/s**). Both lose to llama.cpp b10909 (28.2 tok/s / 872 tok/s). Profiling roots the decode gap in per-kernel dispatch overhead under full CUDA graphs (963 kernels/step, ~19.5 µs floor each, 23 ms idle/step), NOT in the INT4 kernel (~574 GB/s, near bandwidth).

summary: Explained why the generated vLLM row (max-model-len 36864) could not serve a dp-forge spec pipeline, then measured the window arithmetic with a boot matrix (8 arms, boot-log only) and a depth curve (2 arms x 4 depths x 3 reps, 8k to 98k cold prefill) of vllm-radiance 0.9.3 MTP-3 at ctx 114688 against llama.cpp Vulkan Qwen3.8-27B Q4 at ctx 200000. title: Sly radiance 1.6.0 (vLLM docker) · Qwen3.8-27B AMD MXFP4 · fp8 KV — depth curve + growing conversation
takeaway: SlyBase/vllm-sly-radiance **1.6.0** (docker, vLLM 0.31.0) serving **amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4** on one R9700, fp8 KV, ctx 150000, **no speculative decoding** (MEASURED): **prefill 2,845 → 1,500 tok/s** (8k → 136k, k −0.21) — ~2.3–3.2× the repo's earlier llama.cpp/radiance-0.9.3 prefill on the same fixtures — but **decode only 33.8 → 17.9 tok/s** (k −0.23), below llama.cpp+MTP; the drafter is the missing piece. Setup lessons: NVFP4 load peak crashed the desktop (→ boot watchdog), containerd image store ignores docker `data-root`, vLLM 0.31 streams `delta.reasoning`.

title: Sly radiance 1.6.0 (vLLM docker) · Qwen3.8-27B AMD MXFP4 · fp8 KV · DFlash2 k=7 — depth curve + growing conversation
takeaway: Adding the **DFlash2 k=7 drafter** (`syvai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W4A16`) to Sly radiance 1.6.0 + AMD MXFP4 + fp8 KV on one R9700 (one variable vs the no-speculation baseline, MEASURED): **cold decode 33.8 → 136.6 tok/s at 8k (4.0×) and 17.9 → 100.5 at 136k (5.6×)**; in the growing 9-turn conversation decode rises to **~145–203 tok/s at 70–131k** (acceptance 66.9 %, τ 5.68 vs 30.6–52.9 %, τ 3.1–4.7 cold); **prefill unchanged** (±3 %); conversation wall to 131k **184.8 → 108.3 s** and is now 86 % prefill. Decode is no longer depth-bound (verify-step rate k −0.06 vs AR −0.23) but acceptance-bound. Cost: KV pool **433,957 → 345,297 tok** (−20 %, still 2.3 × 150k), prefix-cache granularity 64 → 880 tok, VRAM +400 MiB, GTT at baseline. 0 faults in 29 requests (the baseline's faulting 131k turn passed twice). Beats the repo's older llama.cpp+MTP numbers on both prefill and decode (not like-for-like). OPEN: DFlash vs the image's always-on n-gram lookup draft are not separated; reply text not captured, so Sly #164 repetition cannot be ruled out.

Main result: cold single-stream decode rises from 33.8 to 136.6 tok/s at 8k (4.0x) and from 17.9 to 100.5 at 136k (5.6x) with prefill unchanged within 3 percent; the conversation wall time falls from 184.8 s to 108.3 s, and decode is now set by acceptance (tau) rather than depth. title: Sly radiance 1.6.0 · Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 · fp8 KV · DFlash2 — 170k window filled to the edge: memory over time
takeaway: vLLM (Sly radiance 1.6.0) + MXFP4 + fp8 KV + DFlash2 at **max-model-len 170000**, conversation filled to 150k then grown by hard-thinking turns to **169.3k** (MEASURED): **no memory creep** — device VRAM peaked at **30,259 MiB** (29.55 GiB) during the cold 150k prefill, then stepped down and stayed flat at 29,774 MiB for ~5 min and two conversations; GTT 64–120 MiB (no spill). KV pool **332,822 tok** (11.84 GiB, 1.96 × 170k); one full 170k sequence occupies **51 %** of it (`kv_cache_usage_perc`). Memory is not the limit at util 0.90 — **reliability is**: a 2nd GPU memory fault in the same `radiance_mxfp4_fp8_gemm_atiled` kernel (rep 1, ~156k context) hung the engine 387 s → EngineDead. MXFP4 tally: 2 faults in 84 requests, 2 of 4 serving boots, both in the 2nd deep conversation of a boot. Side finding: novel 1k-token thinking at 150k decodes at **~65 tok/s**; repeated-task turns copy the earlier answer at ~178 tok/s (not representative).
summary: Filled a single 170k window (max-model-len 170000, fp8 KV, util 0.90, DFlash2 k=7 on Sly radiance 1.6.0 MXFP4) to the edge: a cold 150k prefill followed by hard-thinking turns to 169.3k tokens over two conversations, sampling device VRAM and GTT every second. Main result: no memory creep; device VRAM peaked at 30,259 MiB during the cold 150k prefill and then stayed flat at 29,774 MiB, with one full 170k sequence using 51 percent of a 332,822-token KV pool; reliability, not memory, was the limit, as a second GPU memory fault killed the engine after a 387 s hang.
status_note: memory measurements stand; the fault root cause and the not-safe-for-long-runs verdict are superseded by the HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0 fix in 2026-10-23-0023

title: vLLM (Sly radiance MXFP4 + DFlash) GPU memory fault on R9700 — solved by HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0
takeaway: The random HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT (any ROCm kernel, address = a valid pointer with bit 44 cleared) disappears with HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0 (kernel args in host memory instead of device memory written over PCIe) — 3/3 boots × 4 Claude turns clean at full speed (decode med 111–150, prefill med 2.4–3.0k tok/s); not the Sly kernels, not the 7.0.0-38 driver. Now the default in every vLLM profile.
headings: Logical path (what each step ruled in or out)
summary: Root-causing and fixing a random HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT that hit Sly radiance MXFP4 + DFlash2 boots under Claude Code (any kernel, page-not-present), by logging pointers and testing kernel version, ctx, Sly version, the A-tiled path, padding overlays, prefill-only and decode-only splits and warm starts. Main result: the fault address is a valid buffer pointer with bit 44 cleared, and HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0 (kernel arguments in host memory) removed the fault: 3 of 3 boots times 4 Claude turns clean, against faults in about 12 of about 21 earlier boots, with decode median 111-150 tok/s and prefill median 2.4-3.0k tok/s.
status_note: fix confirmed on 3 clean boots plus 1 via llama-swap (small n); kernel 7.0.0-38 gate and llama.cpp retest still open

title: Benchmark: local-agent Ornith vs Haiku on document analysis — R9700 (gfx1201)
takeaway: Local-agent Ornith 1.5 on native Radiance is eligible for high-volume mechanical doc extraction up to about 110k tokens / 7 docs per session (117k: 32/35 facts on the exact line, 0 fabricated, 9/9 planted incidents at 185k context), but not unattended for judgement: on the same 4 reports at depth, two blind passes gave verdicts of 8-9/12 against Haiku high's 11-12/12. Across its 6 deep notes it had 3 critical errors (2 in both Opus passes, 1 found by a later Haiku check), 19 incidents missed and 0 cross-report conflicts found. Haiku medium had the best path recall (43/45) and clean formatting but missed more incidents than high or low. Ornith has no effort levels (only thinking on/off), reasoning replay costs 7.4-9.2k of window per doc, and local-agent.sh loads CLAUDE.md plus 48 tools (33.2k tokens) unless given clean flags.
summary: Compared local Ornith 1.5 on native Radiance 1.16.0 with Haiku 5.5 at effort high, medium and low on document analysis: 4 to 7 repo reports read in one session, fact extraction, incident and path recall, cross-report synthesis, and blind grading by Opus and a later Haiku pass. Main result: Ornith is eligible for mechanical extraction up to about 110k tokens and 7 documents per session (at 117k it put 32 of 35 facts on the cited line, invented none and found 9 of 9 planted incidents at 185k context), but not for unattended judgement (verdicts 8/12 and 9/12 at depth vs Haiku high 12/12 and 11/12).

title: Ornith use cases: what to give it, how much, and how to check it
takeaway: Ornith 1.5 on native Radiance is a good free worker when the task is clear and a script can check the result: JSON to **131k**, code inventory to **88k**, document splitting with **0 lost lines in 6 of 6** runs, tests, renames and clear bug fixes. Draft only for bug classification and code from a spec; never retype text (6k took **480 s**, two more runs didn't finish). Haiku `max` wins on exhaustive lists and path extraction, and Ornith is about **4× faster** on the median task. Mostly n=1. Repeats with 3 sessions in parallel (**1.46×** throughput) make the operator's `dp` prompt the default: a quality tie on 29 of 34 tasks with **17% fewer** generated tokens. Per-profile add-ons don't earn their place, and the `code` allow-list blocks most of Ornith's test commands (7–15 denials per `impl` session).

title: Claude Haiku 5.5: when and how to use it
takeaway: Manual for Claude Haiku 5.5 as a subagent worker and grader next to the local Ornith. Use it where completeness or judgement matters — exhaustive lists (log classes 21/21 at 340k), paths (.94–.97 recall vs Ornith .57–.76), full configs (8/8 vs 4/8), incidents in footnotes and hedged text, retyping text, and blind grading. Don't spend it on mechanical work Ornith ties for free and about 4× faster. Effort is not monotonic on quality: `high` is the default, `low` breaks formats on large input, `medium` lists the fewest incidents, and `max` on a large multi-file job can think past the 128k output limit without writing anything.
summary: Manual for Claude Haiku 5.5 used as a Claude Code subagent (worker and grader) next to a local Ornith 1.5, built from the document-analysis and use-case runs: which jobs are worth Haiku's cost (complete lists, paths, full configurations, incidents, retyping, blind grading), how effort levels change output and format, and the failure modes to guard against. Main result: Haiku listed 21 of 21 error classes in a 340k-token log (Ornith 16 of 21 in one run) but still missed 8-9 incidents across six deep notes at high effort, while effort low broke the line format at six documents and effort max ran past the output limit without writing a file.

title: Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B: when and how to use it
takeaway: Manual for Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B on local Radiance — free, about 4× faster than Haiku on the median task, and reliable where the task is clear and a script checks the result (JSON to 131k, code inventory to 88k, 0 invented facts, every planted fault and labelled incident). Avoid it for exhaustive lists, paths, full configs, incidents told in footnotes or hedged text (0/3 vs Haiku 6/6, not fixed by 12 prompt and brief variants), retyping text, and final verdicts. Thinking is always on and the effort setting does nothing; `dp` appended helps `data` and `code` but hurts `read`; replacing Claude Code's prompt hurts `code`. 3 parallel sessions give 1.46× throughput and fill the card.
summary: Manual for Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B on native Radiance as a free local worker in headless Claude Code, built from the document, use-case and speed runs: what it does reliably (JSON, code inventory, tests, renames, bug fixes, splitting through a manifest), where it fails (paths, exhaustive lists, incidents in prose, retyping, verdicts), its speed and capacity, and which knobs do nothing (effort) or should be kept (sampler, dp prompt on some profiles). Main result: effort settings give identical token counts, retyping a 6k document took 480 s with 69k generated tokens, and decode runs at 219.8 tok/s at 10k context and 174.5 tok/s at 100k.

title: GPU driver stack upgrade runbook — Vulkan (Mesa/RADV) and ROCm on the R9700
takeaway: Runbook for upgrading this box's two GPU stacks — **Vulkan (Mesa RADV via kisak PPA + LunarG loader)** and **ROCm (Radeon apt line)** — which share only the in-kernel `amdgpu` driver. Step-by-step for both, every failure hit during the 2026-09-10 ROCm 7.13→10.0 upgrade with its fix (`pipefail`+SIGPIPE aborts, `cc` shim, exit-0 builds, stale kernel caches, llama-swap `/unload`), rollback, open items (7.13 purge still pending) and sources.

summary: Runbook for upgrading the two GPU userspace stacks on this box, Vulkan (Mesa RADV from the kisak PPA with the LunarG loader) and ROCm (Radeon apt line), which share only the kernel amdgpu driver: pre-upgrade snapshot and baseline, freeing the GPU, the Vulkan procedure (not yet performed), the ROCm 7.13 to 10.0 upgrade of 2026-09-10 with every failure hit and its fix, verification, rollback and open items. Main result: the ROCm upgrade installed 52 packages, removed none and left Mesa untouched, while CASK prefill went from a 1.57x win on ROCm 7.13 to a 47% loss on 10.0, so tuning must be re-measured after every driver change.

title: vLLM track — historical fixes (version/environment-specific)
headings: Related (not yet graduated — same bug family, untested)
summary: Register of version- or environment-specific fixes that were once carried as generic rules and are now historical, with one graduated entry: HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0, which ended a random HSA memory fault on about 12 of 21 boots of Sly radiance MXFP4 with DFlash by moving kernel arguments to host memory, and one candidate for the llama.cpp ROCm -fa on fault. Main result: the variable was a default in the profiles and in CLAUDE.md as a generic ROCm rule, and the current sly-official recipe no longer sets it, so the entry records when it applied and why.

Method is a source review of the hipfire docs plus a read of the box's current state (no ROCm HIP SDK, no Rust, 55 GB free); nothing was run on hipfire. Conclusion: MTP is unavailable for the 27B dense model so DFlash is the speculative path, and the recommended route is a three-phase gate (standalone bench, then manual opencode provider, then llama-swap backend), with the vendor's 203.9 tok/s gfx1201 figure being for a 35B MoE, not the 27B.

summary: Web-research synthesis on llama.cpp and ollama tuning for the R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4) with Qwen3.6 35B-A3B and 27B at 64K, covering -b/-ub batching, flash attention, KV quant, hipBLASLt versus rocBLAS, ROCm versus Vulkan, and ollama's num_batch. No GPU work was done; the community and third-party numbers are directional. The key contrast is our own baseline sweep on b1295, where 35B prefill rose from 529 tok/s at ub32 to 1489 at ub512, against the ub 32/64 folklore, and the community figure of +29% for -b 16384 -ub 2048.

title: llama.cpp --spec-draft-p-min and the MTP path (default, semantics, applicability)
takeaway: ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-07-16 by measurement — the original "p_min is inert on MTP" conclusion (from source-reading) is FALSE on our build. Test campaigns/perf/2026-07-16-0927-mtp-sampler-tax/results/2026-07-16-1111-spec-draft-pmin-mtp/ shows --spec-draft-p-min IS live on the --spec-type draft-mtp path at b9950: raising it 0->0.99 cuts drafted-tok/pass 2.98->0.46, lifts acceptance 69%->100%, changes the output, and LOWERS decode 160->106 t/s. It does NOT reduce run-to-run fluctuation (6/6 distinct replies at every level, both 35B and 27B). Still true: default at our commit is 0.0f (NOT 0.75 — that was the b6000 default; history 0.9→0.75→0.0). Corrected recommendation: do NOT set --spec-draft-p-min for throughput (it costs decode) and it is not a fluctuation remedy; --spec-draft-n-max remains the draft-depth lever (peaks 2-3). Penalty samplers still cost ~2 ms/token host work under MTP; keep them 0 for coding.

summary: Source-reading plus local measurement of llama.cpp --spec-draft-p-min on the MTP path (--spec-type draft-mtp, build b9950), with an erratum that retracts the original claim that p_min is inert on MTP. The measured test (35B-A3B, seed 42) shows p_min is live: raising it from 0.0 to 0.99 cut drafted tokens per pass from 2.98 to 0.46 and raised acceptance from 69% to 100%, but decode fell from 159.9 to 106.5 t/s and it does not reduce run-to-run fluctuation. Corrected recommendation: do not set p_min for throughput, and sweep --spec-draft-n-max instead, where decode peaks at n_max 2-3.

title: Research: Designing a HARD, auto-gradable TypeScript quality benchmark that separates serving configs
takeaway: To make the 27B quality eval DISCRIMINATE, stop chasing pass@1 and stack three orthogonal signals — vitest-pass × tsc-strict × eslint-clean (COMPASS/"Beyond Pass Rate" show compound grading widens model spread and even flips rankings) — on top of a long-context "find+reuse a planted util while obeying top-of-prompt rules" probe. ADOPT the runnable, MIT, jest/vitest test-suites (Exercism-TS 106 + type-challenges 190 tsc-only) for the base tasks; AUTHOR only the ~10-15 constraint-stacked long-context tasks (no existing repo tests retrieval-at-depth × instruction-retention together). Qwen3.6 is native 262K but NO official RULER/needle curve exists — treat effective depth as unknown and measure it ourselves.
headings: 3. Multi-objective grading as the discriminator (the key lever)
summary: Design research for a hard, auto-gradable TypeScript coding benchmark for a 27B model at 64-128K context, aimed at separating temperature and thinking-budget configs when pass@1 saturates. Method was a live multi-source search (Tier-1 repos and papers first, Tier-2 flagged) with 15 numbered findings. Recommendation: adopt the MIT Exercism-TypeScript (~106) and type-challenges (~190) suites as the base set, grade each task as the AND of vitest, tsc strict and eslint, and author the 10-15 constraint-stacked long-context tasks since no existing benchmark combines retrieval at depth with rule retention; the 40-70% pass-rate band is a design target from AgentIF, not a measured result.

takeaway: LLaMA-Factory is production-ready for R9700 (gfx1201); axolotl/torchtune lack official support; bitsandbytes paged optimizers have critical ROCm bug.

title: Research: LLM fine-tuning/training feasibility on the R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB, ROCm 7.x)
takeaway: QLoRA on gfx1201 is FEASIBLE but fragile — official ROCm 7.0.2+ support, LLaMA-Factory + AMD bitsandbytes fork is the one proven path (32B QLoRA @ ~28 GiB precedent on R9700); flash-attn/liger/unsloth broken or unofficial; 27B fits only at short seq; LoRA-16bit/DPO/GRPO on 27B do NOT fit 32 GB; train-while-serve impossible.
headings: What fits in 32 GB (decision table for the finetune loop)
Consequences for the gateway's background finetune loop
summary: Feasibility spike on whether the R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB, ROCm 7.x) can train by QLoRA, LoRA, DPO or GRPO, and what fits in 32 GB, for a background finetune loop. From 14 sources (10 Tier-1), with a decision table of job fits. Conclusion: QLoRA is feasible but fragile on the LLaMA-Factory plus AMD bitsandbytes fork stack (precedent ~28 GiB for 32B QLoRA), 27B fits only in 4-bit at short sequence, 27B LoRA with a bf16 base and 27B DPO or GRPO do not fit, and training cannot run while the 27B is served on the same card.

title: Research: Qwen3.6 sampling, thinking budget & output-variance control (llama.cpp GGUF, R9700)
takeaway: Our campaign's temp 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 / min_p 0 / presence_penalty 0 is EXACTLY Qwen's "thinking mode, precise coding" recommendation — vendor-correct, do not change it. The real finding: Qwen recommends **32,768 output tokens** (81,920 for highly complex problems) while we run `--reasoning-budget 4096` and the model **saturates it every time** (3629–4095 MEASURED) — we have been truncating thinking ~8× below vendor guidance, a plausible driver of the erratic outputs. 16384 is the practical ceiling at 128k depth (32768 does NOT fit ctx 163840). `--reasoning-budget 0` is NOT "non-thinking mode": it forces an immediate end-of-thinking, whereas Qwen's non-thinking recipe (temp 0.7 / top_p 0.80 / presence_penalty 1.5) belongs to the `enable_thinking=false` template path — conflating them confounds budget with sampling. Qwen3.6 docs contain NO greedy-decoding warning and NO variance-reduction guidance beyond presence_penalty for repetition: "lower temp = less variance" is FOLKLORE here. MTP (on in every cell) is a documented output-changing mechanism (llama.cpp #23335, closed) and is an untested variance suspect.

Also found that --reasoning-budget 0 is not the non-thinking template path, that the cards offer no greedy warning or variance guidance, and that MTP is an untested variance suspect.

title: Ornith-1.0-35B & Gemma-4-31B-it-qat — recommended configs + arch facts for R9700 benchmarking
takeaway: Two new models staged in the HF cache. Ornith-1.0-35B is a qwen35moe HYBRID (MEASURED 40 blocks = 10 full-attn KV + 30 SSM linear-attn, **0 nextn/MTP**), native 262144, f16 KV 20 KiB/tok, weights 20.6 GiB → full 262K fits 32 GB; sampling is the Qwen coding recipe (temp 0.6/top_p 0.95/top_k 20), `<think>` blocks, qwen3_xml tools. **MTP is NOT possible for Ornith** (no embedded nextn tensors, no drafter shipped). Gemma-4-31B-it-qat is a gemma4 DENSE hybrid (sliding-window 1024 + global, 60 blocks, per-layer KV-head array), native 262144, QAT-Q4 (UD-Q4_K_XL 16.1 GiB); a thinking model (`<|think|>`/`<|channel>` template CONFIRMED in gguf); sampling temp 1.0/top_p 0.95/top_k 64. **MTP IS possible for Gemma** via a separate 280 MB drafter `mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf` (NOT yet downloaded) + `--spec-type draft-mtp -md <drafter>`. Tooling gap: `gguf_kv.py` cannot size gemma4 (head_count_kv is a per-layer array, not a scalar) — VRAM guard must be set by hand for Gemma until the tool learns gemma4. **UPDATE 2026-07-19 (MEASURED): Gemma deep prefill CRASHES the Vulkan/RADV driver (`vk::DeviceLostError`, GUI-crashing device-loss) at ~65.5k @ctx163840 / ~24.5k @ctx140000 — a DRIVER bug, not memory — but on `BACKEND=rocm` it runs the full depth suite CLEAN (q8_0, ctx150000, n=1: 56.6% TS, 0/5 hard-pass, decode 11.6 t/s). So Gemma→ROCm, Ornith→Vulkan. Gemma emits `<think>` (not `<|channel>`; capture.py splits fine). Ornith (Vulkan) = 62.2% TS n=3.**
summary: Config and architecture facts for two models staged in the HF cache: Ornith-1.0-35B (qwen35moe hybrid, 0 nextn tensors, so MTP is off; f16 KV 20 KiB per token) and Gemma-4-31B-it-qat (gemma4 dense, with a per-layer KV-head array that gguf_kv.py cannot size). The 2026-07-19 update block records that Gemma's deep prefill device-losts RADV on Vulkan at about 65k tokens, while the ROCm build completes a 140k prefill clean at about 11.6 tok/s decode. Sources are HF cards (CLAIMED) and local GGUF headers (MEASURED). Open items before a run are listed in the campaign plan.

title: Deep Dive: KV-cache quantization (q8_0 / fp8) quality at long context
takeaway: 8-bit KV (llama.cpp q8_0, calibrated fp8) is near-lossless at short context (Qwen3 8B q8_0 PPL 7.3195 vs f16 7.3203; Qwen3.5-9B KLD 0.00076) and, on NVIDIA with calibrated or even scale-1.0 fp8, holds on Qwen3.x to 256k-1M (MRCR ~94-98% recovery, Qwen3.5-27B ≤0.7 pt loss). But no evidence exists for our exact stack (hybrid Qwen3.8-27B, ROCm radiance R4D fp8 / Vulkan q8_0) above ~130k. The KV delta (0-3 pts) is far smaller than the model's own context rot (NoLiMa: 11/13 models <50% of baseline at 32k), and in our agentic runs Claude Code's auto-compaction at ~136k is the dominant "forgetting". The RedHat MXFP4 checkpoint ships calibrated per-tensor fp8 k/v scales (MEASURED). Next step: own needle/MRCR at 64k/128k/190k, accept at ≥95% recovery.
headings: How It Works — the two formats we run
summary: Deep-dive on whether 8-bit KV (llama.cpp q8_0 and vLLM fp8) stays near-lossless at long context for the hybrid Qwen3.8-27B on our two engines, from one web-research subagent pass with local checks. Short-context evidence is strong (q8_0 PPL 7.3195 vs f16 7.3203), long-context fp8 evidence exists only on NVIDIA kernels to 256k-1M, and no measurement exists above about 130k on ROCm or Vulkan. Headline: a kernel accumulation bug on Hopper FA3 dropped needle recall at 128k from 91% to 13% before its fix, and the agentic compaction at about 136k dominates forgetting more than KV precision does.

title: Deep Dive (companion): quantization vs reasoning length, Claude Code compaction, agentic run-to-run variance
takeaway: Companion research for the thinking-volume analysis. (1) 4-bit weight-only quantization does not lengthen reasoning traces (Liu et al. 2025: W4G128 lengths ≈ BF16, only W3 / W4A4KV4 lengthen, mostly at 1.5B), so a Q4-vs-MXFP4 thinking gap is not expected from the format; MXFP4 W4A4 recovers less than NVFP4/INT4 on Llama (87.8-93.3% vs 94.7-96.1%), not measured on reasoning models. (2) Claude Code's auto-compact window is set by CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW (100k-1M, capped at the model window); PCT_OVERRIDE can only lower the trigger; compaction keeps ≤5 recent files and turns files >5k tokens into path-only references. (3) Agentic step counts vary run to run (CV ~15% at best, snippet); ~6 runs per arm is established practice.
summary: Companion research to the thinking-volume analysis, covering whether 4-bit weight quantization lengthens reasoning traces, whether MXFP4 W4A4 is weaker than NVFP4 or INT4, how Claude Code's auto-compaction window and threshold are set, and how much run-to-run variance agentic step counts show. Conclusions: 4-bit weight-only quantization does not lengthen reasoning (W4G128 close to BF16), the compaction trigger at about 136k is our own environment configuration, and one run per arm cannot separate a 20% step-count difference (n of about 8 to 9 per arm needed, INFERRED). External figures come from one subagent pass, with snippets flagged.

title: Options Comparison: how much earlier reasoning to replay in long agent sessions (preserve_thinking)
takeaway: Preserving earlier reasoning in agent loops is worth a few points over dropping it all: MiniMax M2 SWE-bench 69.4 vs 67.2, BFCL multi-turn about +2-5% on Qwen3 8B/4B. On search and agent tasks the gain can be large (Tau² 87 vs 64). "Keep all" is not the optimum, though. The only Qwen3.x comparison (Sly 1.9.1) puts keep-newest-only at 25/32 multi-turn tasks, keep-all at 22/32 and drop-all at 17/32. Its no-result (loop) rate is 6/64 for keep-newest vs 35/64 for keep-all. A long-agent paper found full history (0.627) worse than deleting all reasoning (0.718) or entropy-pruning 80% of it (0.738). No published curve exists for keep-last-k with k=2..N. Recommendation for our Qwen3.8-27B Claude Code sessions: keep the newest turn only (k=1, sly2 rule), and test k=2-3 only if recall failures show up. Keep-all is unsafe with Cactus δ>0 and doubles context growth.
summary: Options comparison on how many earlier turns of reasoning to replay in long agent sessions (keep all, keep newest only, keep none), built from vendor and benchmark evidence plus our own W2-08 Claude Code runs. The only Qwen3.x comparison (Sly 1.9.1, vendor-internal) puts keep-newest at 25/32 multi-turn tasks, keep-all at 22/32 and drop-all at 17/32, with loop rates 6/64 against 35/64. Recommendation is keep the newest turn only (k=1, the sly2 rule), with keep-all unsafe when Cactus delta is above 0, though k=1 still looped at delta 0.5 in our runs.

title: RDNA4 / Radeon AI PRO R9700 — lokális LLM optimalizáció (kódolásra)
takeaway: ROCm works on gfx1201 via ollama `rocm_v7_2`; RDNA4 = FP8 native, no FP4 WMMA; 32 GB memory-bound → Q4_K_M optimal; MTP is llama.cpp-only.

3. A ROCm-beállítás, ami megoldotta a „nem látszik" problémát
summary: Hungarian-language note from 2026-07-09 on running local coding models on the R9700 under ROCm and ollama. It finds that the ollama install had no ROCm runner, and that an earlier segfault came from VRAM contention between several ollama instances, not from gfx1201. It argues that the 32 GB card is memory-bound, so Q4 is the optimum; that RDNA4 has native FP8 but no FP4 WMMA; and that MTP needs a direct llama.cpp build. The model shortlist is Qwen3.6 35B-A3B and 27B plus Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B. The figures are the doc's own runs, with no campaign row behind them.

title: vLLM on RDNA4 (gfx1201): AITER, FP8, and the Qwen3.6-27B hybrid arch — current status
takeaway: On gfx1201/RDNA4, AITER's C++/ASM kernels don't run (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 required) and gfx1201 is missing from AITER's arch table → FP8 silently falls back to FP32 (~18–22 vs ~35–40 tok/s). vLLM supports the Qwen3.6-27B hybrid arch, but FP8 is gated to NVIDIA Ada/Hopper — so the AITER/Triton/unified-attn env-vars are non-viable on the R9700 today; treat any vLLM spike as gated on a load-test first.

title: Why Qwen3.5-35B-A3B decodes at ~16 t/s on Sly radiance 1.9.1 / R9700, and what would make it fast
takeaway: The 35B decodes at ~16 t/s on Sly 1.9.1 because its MoE experts run through the vLLM OCP-MX EMULATION backend, which dequantizes ALL 256 experts of every layer to bf16 on every forward pass (~96 GB of memory traffic per decode step, INFERRED, vs ~180 ms/step MEASURED). The step is ~4-5x slower than the 27B's (37-44 ms), and acceptance (2.9 vs 3.7 tokens/step) explains only ~1.3x. No native MXFP4 MoE backend can run on gfx1201 (every one is gated on gfx950/gfx942/gfx1250/CUDA). Sly's own 35B-A3B MoE recipe (MiniCPM-V 4.7, GPTQ W4A16 + a tuned R9700 int4 MoE config) is CLAIMED at 169 t/s decode, so a W4A16 int4 checkpoint is the realistic fast path. FP8 does not fit 32 GB. 200 t/s is not demonstrated for any 35B on this card; ~120-170 t/s is.

title: Configuring vLLM + Radiance for a 35B-A3B on one R9700, and whether anything reaches 2x the 27B
takeaway: Switching amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 from the EMULATION MoE backend to --moe-backend triton_unfused lifts DFlash K=7 decode from 16.6 to 110 t/s at 10k (6.6x, MEASURED), which confirms EMULATION as the root cause, but it only reaches parity with the 27B, not 2x. CORRECTED: this report's estimate that nothing could reach ~200 t/s was wrong. It missed Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B w4a8 on native Radiance, later measured at 220 t/s.
summary: Confirms the EMULATION diagnosis of 2026-11-04-1630 by measurement: on Sly 1.9.1, --moe-backend triton_unfused with DFlash K=7 takes the 35B-A3B MXFP4 from 16.6 tok/s to 110.2 at 10k (6.6x), and gives 93 and 67 at 50k and 100k. That does not reach 2x the 27B. The doc's own 'no alternative reaches about 200 tok/s' verdict was wrong: its correction box points to Ornith 1.5 w4a8 on native Radiance at 219.8 tok/s at 10k, measured in a separate findings doc. Correctness and MTP on the unfused backend are untested.
